title: Half the Melody Is in the Other Room
sunoStyleTag: Reed Hocket Garage (TÁROGATÓ + UK GARAGE / 2-STEP + CIMBALOM + BASS VIOLA, 128–136 BPM). Make the main melodic identity a true acoustic hocket: divide hooks note-by-note or two- to three-note cell-by-cell between dark, breathy tárogató and bright hammered cimbalom so neither instrument performs the complete line alone. Tárogató should use clear reed edge, key noise, short bends, narrow slides, breath pickups, and compact modal phrases rather than long heroic solos. Cimbalom should answer with dry single notes, muted dead-strokes, sparse dyads, restrained rolls, and hand damping. Use bass viola for bowed pedals, pizzicato fifths, and short glissandi that alternate with electronic sub instead of continuously doubling it. Add understated brushed snare, shell taps, and small frame percussion as a human shadow inside machine-drum gaps. Use short low-feedback tape delay only to stitch unfinished phrase endings between instruments. Harmonic language: Dorian/Aeolian, open fifths, minor 7ths, suspended 2nds, occasional Hungarian-minor color, slow two- to four-chord loops. Keep production dry, tactile, woody, metallic, and rhythmically precise with moderate swing and natural microtiming. Avoid trap hats, EDM drops, lush pads, orchestral strings, constant vocal chops, generic Balkan wedding-band clichés, and cinematic folk fusion.
